=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12358-12371 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When no implementation PR is resolved because STALL_IMPL_PR_FAILURE_REASON is not_implementation_pr, the standalone attempt_merge path still reports an attempted merge and increments recovery state even though no merge occurred.
  WHY: Operators receive a misleading Telegram notification and the recovery budget may be consumed; severity disagreement exists, with minimax rating this MAJOR and deepseek rating it NIT.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10296-10312 and 9822-9830 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The managed dispatch_rb_judge branch does not set an equivalent STALL_RECOVERY_EFFECTIVE_ACTION label when implementation-PR lookup is inconclusive.
  WHY: Downstream observers cannot distinguish this skipped dispatch from a generic failed dispatch.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:test_resolver_branch_lookup_is_pipefail_safe (asserts literal source string) | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The pipefail-safety test checks for a literal source substring rather than reproducing the multi-line SIGPIPE failure mode.
  WHY: A regression in actual pipefail behavior could pass while the string assertion remains present.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12489-12540 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The standalone dispatch_rb_judge path does not defensively revalidate STALL_IMPL_PR_JSON before dispatching after resolver success.
  WHY: Correctness relies entirely on the helper’s current non-empty-JSON success contract.
- tests/test_linked_pr_implementation_guard.py:test_resolver_logs_conventional_branch_fetch_failures_distinctly (lines ~285-298) | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The resolver contract does not document the silent miss case when branch lookup is empty and the cross-reference walk is skipped.
  WHY: Operators may misinterpret the absence of STALL_LINKED_PR_REJECTED as a fetch failure.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:11256 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The branch lookup uses head -n1 without sorting, so multiple conventional-branch matches may produce non-deterministic PR selection.
  WHY: Recovery actions could target the wrong implementation PR.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12296 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The fetch uses a DWIM refspec that may be ambiguous when a tag and branch share the same name.
  WHY: Git could fetch the wrong object and break recovery logic.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:11258-11277 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: STALL_IMPL_PR_FAILURE_REASON is not checked consistently before recovery actions in all error paths.
  WHY: A PR fetch failure could allow destructive actions or incorrectly consume recovery budget.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3197 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The change from §14 audit to §15 audit is documentation-only and does not affect runtime behavior.
  WHY: It does not fail at runtime.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10184-10191 and dispatch call at line 10226 (managed `skip` case, healthy-PR redirect), reachable via `execute_stall_recovery_action skip` | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: The managed skip-case healthy-PR redirect dispatches against the mention-based PR lookup instead of the verified implementation-PR resolver.
  WHY: An unrelated mentioning PR can receive review-blocked-judge actions, recreating the wrong-target recovery bug.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12358-12367 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When `_resolve_issue_implementation_pr` conclusively fails with `STALL_IMPL_PR_FAILURE_REASON=not_implementation_pr` (no verified implementation PR), `merge_pr` is empty and control reaches the `else` branch. That branch posts the Telegram message "Standalone stall recovery: attempted merge retry for ready-to-merge issue" even though no merge was attempted and no implementation PR exists.
  WHY: An operator triaging a stuck `ai:ready-to-merge` issue receives a false signal that a merge retry was executed, when in fact the recovery action found no implementation PR and performed no merge.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines 10296-10312 (managed dispatch_rb_judge) and lines 9822-9830 (managed retrigger_review) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The managed `dispatch_rb_judge` branch sets no equivalent `STALL_RECOVERY_EFFECTIVE_ACTION` label when `_resolve_issue_implementation_pr` returns inconclusive.
  WHY: Downstream observers cannot distinguish the action from a normal dispatch path or other skip reasons.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:test_resolver_branch_lookup_is_pipefail_safe (asserts literal source string) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The test asserts a literal substring and does not actually exercise pipefail safety with a stub returning multiple lines.
  WHY: A regression that drops the `|| true` or moves it inside `head` might still pass the assertion.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:attempt_merge block, lines 12358-12371 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When `merge_pr` is empty and the failure reason is `not_implementation_pr`, the else branch still calls `tg_notify_issue` with "Standalone stall recovery: attempted merge retry for ready-to-merge issue" and sets `STALL_RECOVERY_SHOULD_INCREMENT="true"`.
  WHY: Operators see "attempted merge retry" warnings although no merge was attempted because no implementation PR resolved.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:standalone dispatch_rb_judge block, lines 12489-12540 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The dispatch path does not revalidate cached JSON before invoking `_dispatch_review_for_conflicts`.
  WHY: The path relies entirely on the helper's success contract.
- tests/test_linked_pr_implementation_guard.py:test_resolver_logs_conventional_branch_fetch_failures_distinctly (lines ~285-298) | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The test does not cover the case where branch lookup is empty and the cross-ref walk is skipped.
  WHY: The silent miss is by design but undocumented in the resolver contract header comment.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:11256 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The pipeline uses `head -n1` without sorting, which could return non-deterministic results when multiple PRs match the conventional branch name pattern.
  WHY: In a race condition or when multiple implementation PRs exist for the same issue, the resolver could pick the wrong PR.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12296 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The fetch uses a DWIM (Do What I Mean) refspec without explicit `refs/heads/` prefix, which could be ambiguous if a tag and branch share the same name.
  WHY: Git fetch ambiguity could cause the wrong object to be fetched, breaking the recovery logic.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:11258-11277 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The function sets `STALL_IMPL_PR_FAILURE_REASON` but doesn't consistently check it before proceeding with recovery actions in all code paths.
  WHY: In edge cases where PR fetch fails, the recovery logic might still attempt destructive actions (push/merge) instead of skipping, consuming recovery budget incorrectly.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3197 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Documentation-only change that doesn't affect runtime behavior.
  WHY: It doesn't fail at runtime; this is a documentation update.
=== END FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines 10184-10191 and dispatch call at line 10226 (managed `skip` case, healthy-PR redirect), reachable via `execute_stall_recovery_action skip` | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `skip` case's healthy-PR redirect still resolves its review-blocked-judge dispatch target from `STALL_MANAGED_LINKED_PR_CACHE` / `_issue_cross_ref_pr_number_last` (`_skip_pr_num`) instead of the new `_resolve_issue_implementation_pr` helper.
  WHY: A managed issue can redirect review-blocked judge actions to an unrelated PR that only mentions the issue.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k3 ===
